name: Strava
one_line: Records runs and rides via GPS and drops them into a social feed of kudos, segments and challenges.
audience: Runners and cyclists who train regularly and want social accountability
notable_metric: Named best Apple Watch app in the 2025 App Store Awards; subscription $11.99/mo or $79.99/yr

name: MyFitnessPal
one_line: Food and calorie diary with a huge barcode-scannable food database plus macro targets.
audience: General consumers tracking weight and macros
notable_metric: Acquired Cal AI in March 2026

name: Cal AI
one_line: Point your phone at a plate of food and it returns calories and macros from the photo.
audience: 15-25 year olds who found manual calorie logging too tedious
notable_metric: 15M+ downloads and $30M+ annual revenue in under two years; built by two 18-year-olds

name: Whoop
one_line: Screenless 24/7 strap that scores daily recovery, strain and sleep from HR and HRV.
audience: Serious athletes and training-obsessed adults

name: Oura
one_line: Smart ring that tracks sleep stages, temperature and readiness and reports a daily score.
audience: Sleep and longevity-focused consumers who dislike wrist wearables

name: Sleep Cycle
one_line: Phone-microphone sleep tracker with a smart alarm that wakes you in your lightest sleep phase.
audience: iPhone owners who want sleep data without buying hardware
notable_metric: Cited as the most popular consumer sleep app on iPhone in 2026 roundups

name: RISE (Rise Science)
one_line: Computes your accumulated sleep debt and circadian energy peaks and schedules your day around them.
audience: Knowledge workers who feel tired despite sleeping enough

name: AutoSleep
one_line: Apple Watch sleep tracker that requires no button presses and writes straight into Apple Health.
audience: Apple Watch owners wanting one-time-purchase sleep tracking

name: JEFIT
one_line: Strength-training logger with 1,400+ demonstrated exercises and sets/reps/weight history.
audience: Gym lifters following structured resistance programs
notable_metric: 20 million users; 42,000+ five-star ratings; $14.99/mo or $71.99/yr

name: Hevy
one_line: Minimal workout logger with routines, rest timers and a light social following feed.
audience: Indie-leaning gym-goers who found JEFIT and Strong bloated

name: Zwift
one_line: Turns an indoor trainer into a multiplayer virtual world where you race other riders in real time.
audience: Indoor cyclists and triathletes training through winter

name: Eight Sleep Pod
one_line: Mattress cover that actively heats and cools each side of the bed and tracks sleep stages.
audience: Couples with mismatched sleep temperatures and high-spend biohackers

name: Flo
one_line: Period and ovulation tracker that predicts cycles and flags symptom patterns.
audience: Women tracking menstrual and fertility cycles
notable_metric: Women's health was ~140M downloads as a health subgenre in 2025

name: Finch: Self-Care Pet
one_line: A virtual bird grows when you complete small self-care tasks and mood check-ins.
audience: Young adults managing anxiety and low motivation between therapy sessions

name: Headspace
one_line: Guided meditation, sleepcasts and short mindfulness courses on a daily cadence.
audience: Mainstream consumers new to meditation

name: Calm
one_line: Sleep stories, meditations and breathing exercises built around a nightly wind-down.
audience: Adults with sleep-onset trouble and stress

name: Skinive AI: Skin Scanner
one_line: Photograph a mole or skin lesion and get an at-home risk read plus mole-map progress tracking.
audience: People monitoring moles and skin changes between dermatologist visits

name: Impakt: AI Coach
one_line: Camera-based AI coach that watches your form rep by rep and pays rewards for completed workouts.
audience: Home exercisers who need form feedback and extrinsic motivation

name: Rosebud
one_line: AI journal that reads your entries and replies with reflective prompts, linking today's entry to past ones.
audience: Therapy-adjacent adults doing structured self-reflection

name: Dayora
one_line: Voice journaling app you can talk with, not just at — it responds and connects entries over time.
audience: People who journal by speaking rather than typing
notable_metric: Cited as the only free talk-back voice journal in 2026 comparisons

name: Day One
one_line: Long-running private journal with photo, location and on-this-day resurfacing.
audience: Committed personal journalers on Apple platforms

name: Voicenotes
one_line: Record a spoken brain dump and it transcribes, summarises and lets you query your own notes.
audience: People who think out loud — commuters, walkers, founders

name: Duolingo
one_line: Gamified bite-size language lessons driven by streaks, leagues and push notifications.
audience: Casual language learners across all ages

name: Speak
one_line: Speaking-first language course where an AI tutor holds unscripted dialogue and corrects you live.
audience: Beginners who want a curriculum plus conversation reps

name: Langua
one_line: Open-ended AI conversation practice that corrects grammar in real time without breaking the flow.
audience: Intermediate learners plateaued between phrasebook and fluency
notable_metric: Ranked top overall AI language app in 2026 roundups

name: MeloLingua
one_line: Story-based language learning with pronunciation feedback on each spoken line.
audience: Learners who want narrative context instead of flashcard drills

name: Babbel
one_line: Structured, expert-designed 10-15 minute grammar-forward lessons around real-life dialogue.
audience: Adults who want a syllabus rather than gamification

name: Busuu
one_line: CEFR-aligned language courses with corrections from native-speaker community members.
audience: Learners working toward a certifiable proficiency level

name: Brilliant
one_line: Interactive math, CS and science problem sets you solve rather than watch.
audience: Self-directed adult learners and STEM-curious professionals

name: Khanmigo
one_line: Khan Academy's AI tutor that Socratically walks students through problems instead of giving answers.
audience: K-12 students, parents and teachers

name: Anki
one_line: Open-source spaced-repetition flashcards with a scheduler that surfaces cards just before you forget.
audience: Medical students, language learners, exam crammers

name: MapQuest
one_line: Turn-by-turn navigation and maps app.
audience: US drivers
notable_metric: #1 top free US iPhone app as of 2026-09-03

name: Vinted
one_line: Peer-to-peer marketplace for buying and selling second-hand clothing.
audience: Gen Z and millennial secondhand fashion buyers and sellers
notable_metric: #3 top free US iPhone app as of 2026-09-03

name: Scanner Pro (Readdle)
one_line: Phone document scanner that runs OCR and, since iOS 26, translation entirely on device.
audience: Professionals scanning receipts, contracts and forms with privacy concerns

name: Genius Scan
one_line: Long-established mobile scanner with AI-generated file naming added in its 2026 update.
audience: Consumers and small businesses digitising paper
notable_metric: Over 20 million users

name: Microsoft Translator
one_line: Free translation across 100+ languages with downloadable offline packs and two-way conversation mode.
audience: Travellers and multilingual households
notable_metric: 4.75-star average; named best iPhone translator app of 2026

name: Notion
one_line: Block-based workspace that merges docs, databases and wikis, now with AI query over your own pages.
audience: Students, freelancers and small teams organising life and work

name: Obsidian
one_line: Local-first Markdown notes on your own disk with bidirectional links and a graph view.
audience: Researchers, writers and privacy-minded PKM users
notable_metric: Cited as the leading local-first knowledge tool in 2026 roundups

name: Tana
one_line: AI-native outliner where voice notes, tasks and meetings auto-link into a structured graph.
audience: Heavy note-takers and knowledge workers
notable_metric: #2 product of the year on Product Hunt's 2025 leaderboard

name: Screen Studio
one_line: Mac screen recorder that auto-produces polished zoom-and-pan videos with instant shareable links.
audience: Indie makers, PMs and creators making product demos
notable_metric: #1 product of the year on Product Hunt's 2025 leaderboard

name: NotebookLM
one_line: Upload your own sources and get grounded answers plus an auto-generated two-host audio overview.
audience: Students and researchers digesting document sets
notable_metric: Popularised the AI audio-overview format later copied by Adobe, Amazon, ElevenLabs, Meta and Spotify

name: Sunsama
one_line: Daily planner that forces you to pull tasks from your tools into a realistic, time-boxed day.
audience: Overcommitted knowledge workers fighting task-list sprawl

name: Structured
one_line: Visual day planner that lays tasks, calendar events and reminders on a single vertical timeline.
audience: ADHD-leaning consumers who need the day drawn out

name: Saner.AI
one_line: AI assistant that ingests notes and email and answers by voice about what you need to do next.
audience: ADHD and neurodivergent knowledge workers
notable_metric: Ranked first in 2026 AI voice-assistant comparison roundups

name: Huckleberry
one_line: Baby tracker that predicts the next optimal nap window from logged sleep patterns.
audience: Parents of infants fighting sleep regressions

name: Napper
one_line: Sleep-first baby app with nap suggestions, soundscapes and sleep education.
audience: New parents wanting nap timing without a full tracking system

name: Nara Baby
one_line: Free, ad-free manual tracker for feeds, diapers, sleep and postpartum recovery.
audience: Budget-conscious new parents who reject subscriptions

name: Robin Baby
one_line: Voice-first newborn tracker — say what happened and it logs it, then answers questions about the day.
audience: Parents holding a baby with one hand who cannot tap through a form

name: Neela
one_line: Caregiving assistant you talk to like a friend; it remembers appointments, notes and documents without manual logging.
audience: Family caregivers managing an ageing parent's care

name: Medisafe
one_line: Medication reminder that alerts a designated family member when a dose is missed and flags drug interactions.
audience: Older adults on complex regimens and their remote family

name: Carely
one_line: Shared care-coordination hub that keeps family and professional caregivers on one update thread.
audience: Families splitting dementia caregiving across siblings and aides

name: Life360
one_line: Family location-sharing map with driving reports, crash detection and place alerts.
audience: Parents of teens and multi-generation households

name: Zigazoo
one_line: Moderated short-video social network for kids where every post answers a prompt challenge.
audience: Kids under 13 and their parents seeking a safe TikTok substitute
notable_metric: $17M Series A (June 2022); ~$21M raised total

name: Lovevery App
one_line: Stage-matched child development activities, research summaries and live expert Q&As.
audience: Parents of children 0-5 following developmental play
notable_metric: $100M Series C closed June 2021

name: Monarch Money
one_line: Aggregates all accounts into one budgeting dashboard built for couples with shared access.
audience: Ex-Mint users and couples budgeting jointly
notable_metric: Most-cited direct Mint replacement; founded by former Mint developers

name: YNAB
one_line: Zero-based budgeting where every dollar is assigned a job before it can be spent.
audience: People willing to do real budgeting work to get out of paycheck-to-paycheck
notable_metric: $109/yr or $14.99/mo; free for college students for 12 months

name: Copilot Money
one_line: Apple-only money tracker with automatic transaction categorisation and clean spending charts.
audience: Apple-ecosystem users who want a design-led Mint replacement

name: Rocket Money
one_line: Finds and cancels forgotten subscriptions and negotiates bills on your behalf.
audience: Consumers leaking money to recurring charges
notable_metric: Offers a free tier with basic budgeting

name: Quicken Simplifi
one_line: Lightweight spending plan with a projected cash-flow view for the rest of the month.
audience: Mint refugees wanting the cheapest full-featured replacement

name: Wispr Flow
one_line: System-wide dictation that turns spoken rambling into cleanly formatted text in any app.
audience: Writers, developers and anyone who types slower than they talk

name: superwhisper
one_line: Mac dictation app that can run Whisper models fully on-device with no cloud round trip.
audience: Privacy-conscious Mac users doing heavy dictation

name: Pi
one_line: Conversational AI built for emotionally supportive back-and-forth rather than task completion.
audience: People who want a calm thinking partner rather than a work assistant
notable_metric: Reached roughly a million users before Inflection pivoted to enterprise in 2024

name: Character.AI
one_line: Chat with user-created personas — fictional characters, historical figures, original creations.
audience: Teens and young adults doing roleplay and story chat
notable_metric: Grew past 20 million monthly users before 2026 lawsuits, settlements and mandatory face-scan age verification reshaped the platform

name: Replika
one_line: A single persistent AI companion with relationship-style memory, voice calls and roleplay.
audience: Lonely or socially isolated adults seeking a consistent confidant

name: Nomi
one_line: AI companions with long-term memory tuned for continuity across months of conversation.
audience: Users who found Replika's memory and filters too limiting

name: Kindroid
one_line: Deeply customisable AI companion with voice calls, AI-generated selfies and granular personality shaping.
audience: Power users who want to author a companion rather than accept a default

name: PocketPal AI
one_line: Free open-source app that downloads and runs small LLMs entirely on your phone, offline.
audience: Privacy-focused and offline users on modern phones
notable_metric: Phi-4 Mini at ~10-15 tokens/sec on iPhone 16 Pro; needs 6GB+ RAM

name: Private LLM
one_line: Paid on-device chat app running 140+ open models on iPhone, iPad and Mac with Siri and Shortcuts hooks.
audience: Apple users who want local AI wired into system automations
notable_metric: $4.99 one-time; 140+ models; Metal and Neural Engine accelerated

name: Locally AI
one_line: iOS app for running MLX and LM Studio-compatible models locally on Apple silicon.
audience: Technical iPhone/iPad users experimenting with local models

name: Ollama
one_line: One-command local model runner that made desktop offline LLMs approachable for non-engineers.
audience: Prosumers and developers running AI on their own machine

name: Meta Wearables Device Access Toolkit
one_line: SDK letting third parties push real-time overlays and micro-apps into the Ray-Ban Display's in-lens screen, driven by frame taps or Neural Band input.
audience: Developers building hands-busy glanceable apps for smart glasses
notable_metric: Developer preview announced 2026-05-14; native Swift/Kotlin SDKs plus a web path

name: Strava for Meta glasses
one_line: Overlays live run and ride performance stats onto glasses-captured video and pairs Meta AI glasses to your Strava account.
audience: Runners and cyclists recording POV workouts on smart glasses
